packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-20 -- first reader, blind image-only reading (unverified)
Exposure: no identification or prior reading of this record was in my context.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overview image-001.jpg; face A)
- Photograph of six separate parchment fragments on black ground, with colour checker, mm scale, and a plastic spatula. Grey boxes mask shelfmark labels.
- (a) Two small narrow strips upper-left (approx. 2x4 cm and 2x5 cm). The upper one appears mostly blank on this side with a pencil note; the lower one carries ends of lines of a text column at its right edge (e.g. "...as/tes/..." line ends).
- (b) Large landscape fragment top-centre/right (approx. 13 x 8.5 cm): small dense gothic textualis, two columns visible, plus a narrow column of line-ends at the far left (so probably a bifolium/strip crossing a fold or the end of a column of a preceding page). Text browned and partly abraded; small red mark mid-column (rubric/paraph?). Two wormholes in lower centre.
- (c) Fragment mounted on white card lower-left: two narrow strips of the same small dense gothic textual script, separated by a gap (a thin white fill), possibly one column split in two.
- (d) Narrow vertical strip centre-bottom (approx. 3.5 x 11 cm): small gothic text column, with a coloured (blue/green?) enlarged initial "h"? partway down on a stained patch.
- (e) Large portrait fragment right (approx. 11 x 18.5 cm): heavily ruled with many fine horizontal rulings, sparse text in a larger, more cursive hand at the top and in scattered short entries in the right half; lower part mostly blank ruled. Likely a different manuscript (or a register/notes), not main-text-with-commentary.
- Tentative: (b), (c), (d) and the lower strip of (a) share a small dense textualis of the same type; (e) is a different, looser hand.
- Tiles: image-002..010 appear to be a 3x3 grid of native-resolution tiles over this overview (row 1: 002-004, row 2: 005-007, row 3: 008-010). Face B overview is image-011 with tiles 012-020.

TILE image-002.jpg (upper-left; the two small strips (a))
Observation: the pencil label is visible ("Stams, STA, Frag. 104_6r" on upper strip; "...frag. 104_5r" on lower strip -- modern shelf notes, not text). Written text sits only at the right edge of each strip: these are the starts of lines of a column whose remainder is cut away (the strips are mostly margin). Text in the upper strip is faint/offset-like, partly under tape at top.

Observation: fragment (b) shows, from left: line-ENDS of a column (left col., right part only, ~23 lines visible, left edge cut), then a wide blank margin with a vertical fold/crease (gutter), then line-BEGINNINGS of a further column (right col.). So the strip crosses the gutter of an opened bifolium (two pages). Pencil label "Stams, STA, Frag. 104-2r" (modern). Ruling visible as fine drypoint/lead lines. Small gothic textualis, heavy abbreviation, punctus with medial dots. A red paraph-like mark at right col. ~l.10. Text much browned/abraded; middle of right column very faint.
